facts.text: Hanover was chartered July 4 1761 by Governor Benning Wentworth, with its first European settlers arriving from Connecticut in 1765‑66.
Dartmouth College, founded 1769 beside Hanover’s town common, sits on “the Plain,” a mile from the Connecticut River.
Baker Library in Hanover houses José Clemente Orozco’s 3,200‑sq‑ft mural, “The Epic of American Civilization,” a national historic landmark.
The Hood Museum’s 2018 expansion added five galleries, now showcasing 70,000 objects including a significant Native American art collection.
Hanover sits on the Upper Connecticut River, a scenic two‑hour drive from Boston and three hours from Providence via I‑93 and I‑89.
Moose Mountain’s north peak, the highest point in Hanover, rises to 2,313 feet, offering sweeping views of the valley.
